summary:
Nothing here changes the picture. The REMAINING GAPS ranking survives intact — no gap dissolves and no new gap appears. Of the 71 newly-verified FALSE/PARTIAL claims, the overwhelming majority are staleness against operator notes pinned at 823bc34/5597814 (sticky sessions, quota-header mining, escalation ladder, doc-block transcoding, retirement seed, process-safety-net/secret-file-acl/think-tags), and the synthesis already records every one of those under DRIFT 15 and RECOMMENDED 5. The remaining items are either freellmapi-internal facts with no llm-relay consequence, or one-shot runtime measurements (suite counts, byte sizes, fetch counts) that no source read can settle.

Two of the newly-verified "corrections" are themselves wrong, and I caught both by going back to source — they are the only two that would have moved a conclusion, and neither survives. (1) The claim that llm-relay "does not gate on tools at materialization ... no code filters a candidate on capability" is false: C:\Code\llm-relay\src\dynamic-pools.ts:220 excludes any entry whose `supportsTools === false` from dynamic-pool membership. Gap 4 stands exactly as the synthesis wrote it, scoped to vision. (2) The claim that freellmapi "has no credential-fault axis separate from health" is false: C:\Code\freellmapi\server\src\lib\fallback-loop.ts:1118 branches on `isKeyAuthError` into `recordAuthFailure` (key-fatal, rotate-and-revalidate, explicitly not a request failure), with a persisted per-key `status='invalid'` surfaced at routes/status.ts:123. Adding a credential-axis bullet to REVERSE would have been a false claim.

Two genuine precision corrections to the synthesis, neither changing a verdict: the REVERSE section's "llm-relay has no counters at all and is purely reactive" is literally untrue (call/token/failure counters exist), and the `freeOnly` guard is not simply opt-in — an unset flag defaults ON for offload-rerouted traffic. The REJECT on quota ledgers and RECOMMENDED item 3 both stand, with sharper wording.

The DOC AUDIT headline "0 FALSE out of 128" is correctly scoped and survives verbatim; the 5 new FALSEs all fall outside that set. No new gap is reportable — every freellmapi capability newly confirmed in this batch (quirks registry, response cache, structured-output healing, reasoning-effort mapping, context handoff, client profiles) either already sits in the synthesis's REJECT block or fails the same rubric tests for the same reasons: a per-model quirks/effort table is the platform-keyed table §5 already rejected (rubric 3, one place per policy), context handoff has the relay authoring conversation content (repair boundary), and client_profiles — correctly read as per-client minted keys plus server-enforced system prompts — is credential custody, ruled out by the owner-ratified "credentials stay user-operated" invariant at docs/project-goals.md:86-96. Stating that invariant application out loud, as that section requires.

materialFindings.finding: The newly-verified correction claiming llm-relay never filters candidates on tool capability is itself FALSE. Re-checked at source: dynamic pool membership is filtered on the tools signal.
materialFindings.evidence: C:\Code\llm-relay\src\dynamic-pools.ts:218-221 — `const usable = ranked.filter((entry) => !excluded.has(specOfTarget(entry.target)) && entry.fitness.signals.supportsTools !== false)`. `usable` is the input to both the in-band set (:222-224) and the degrade tail (:245-256), so a model the snapshot states cannot use tools is admitted to no band of any dynamic pool. The signal is sourced exact-match-only at :53 via the `hit?.match === "exact"` guard at :39. It is separately a ranking input at src\benchmarks.ts:210 (`toolFit`), which is what the chunk verifier saw and mistook for the whole story.
materialFindings.affects: REMAINING GAPS item 4 ("Vision capability is never a routing input"), and by extension whether a broader "no capability gating at all" gap should replace it
materialFindings.correction: Keep gap 4 exactly as written, including its anchor `src/dynamic-pools.ts:220` — that anchor is correct and is the precedent the vision proposal should copy. Do NOT broaden it to tools. The one nuance worth adding to the gap text: the filter runs at materialization over catalog-DISCOVERED members only, so a hand-written static pool and the `preferred` prefix (:216-217) bypass it — which is an argument for keeping any vision flag in the same place rather than adding a request-time check.

materialFindings.finding: The newly-verified correction claiming freellmapi has no credential-fault axis separate from health is FALSE. freellmapi has a key-scoped auth axis that is explicitly not a health failure.
materialFindings.evidence: C:\Code\freellmapi\server\src\lib\fallback-loop.ts:1118-1127 — `if (isKeyAuthError(err)) { /* KEY-fatal, not request-fatal: rotate past the bad key and revalidate it immediately instead of 502-ing while healthy routes sit idle. */ recordAuthFailure(route, hooks.state); ... continue; }`, a branch taken before `isRetryableError` at :1128. Classifier at lib\error-classify.ts:208-224 (401, plus key-specific wording on a 400; a 403 deliberately stays model-forbidden). Persisted per-key state surfaced at routes\status.ts:123 and routes\health.ts:20 (`status = 'invalid'`). llm-relay's counterpart is src\circuit-breaker.ts:481-528 (`recordCredentialFault`/`hasCredentialFault`, 401/403, demote-not-trip).
materialFindings.affects: REVERSE, the "what llm-relay has that freellmapi lacks" bullet list
materialFindings.correction: Do not add a credential-axis bullet to REVERSE. Both systems separate credential faults from health; they differ only in scope keying (llm-relay per deployment with a 5-minute TTL, freellmapi per key with immediate revalidation) — a design difference, not a capability gap in either direction.

materialFindings.finding: The REVERSE section overstates llm-relay's position in freellmapi's favour: "llm-relay has no counters at all and is purely reactive" is not true as written.
materialFindings.evidence: C:\Code\llm-relay\src\ping\runtime-telemetry.ts:19-24 defines `totalCalls`/`successCalls`/`totalLatencyMs`/`totalCompletionTokens`, incremented per request at :107 and read for scoring at :143-157; src\circuit-breaker.ts:17,429,464 keeps `consecutiveFailures` and trips on it at `MAX_FAILURES_BEFORE_TRIP` (:96). Both are surfaced in the candidate table (src\candidates.ts:363,379-381).
materialFindings.correction: Reword to the true distinction: llm-relay counts what already happened and uses it for ranking and breaker state; it keeps no PRE-DISPATCH quota ledger and no in-flight leases, so nothing gates a request before it is sent. The REJECT verdict on porting the ledger is unchanged and its reasoning is untouched (free providers publish no limits to meter against; a second quota policy beside the breaker; the credentials-stay-user-operated invariant).

materialFindings.finding: `freeOnly` is not simply opt-in — an unset flag is ON for offload-rerouted traffic and OFF for a directly addressed pool.
materialFindings.evidence: C:\Code\llm-relay\src\server.ts:1457-1458 — `function freeOnlyApplies(rule: { freeOnly?: boolean }, rerouted: boolean): boolean { return rule.freeOnly ?? rerouted; }`, called at :440 as `(subSpec !== null || addressesPool) && freeOnlyApplies(offloadRule(cfg, requestClient), subSpec !== null)`. The split default is deliberate and documented at src\config.ts:1364-1369, which stores the field EXACTLY as configured so unset and explicit-false stay distinguishable; src\dynamic-pools.ts:174 also calls it "(default ON)".
materialFindings.affects: RECOMMENDED NEXT item 3 (render `freeOnly` in `offload status`), and the REVERSE bullet describing the freeOnly guard
materialFindings.correction: Item 3 must render the EFFECTIVE value, not the raw field — an absent `freeOnly` is not "off", it is "on for rerouted traffic, off for a directly addressed pool", and printing the bare optional would be a new transparency bug rather than a fix. This makes the item slightly more than cosmetic: today an operator cannot tell from `offload status` whether a lane may spend money.

materialFindings.finding: The DOC AUDIT headline is correctly scoped and survives, but the across-all-claims figure is not zero FALSE.
materialFindings.evidence: All 5 FALSE verdicts in the new batch fall outside the 128 adopted/skipped/deferred claims: 3 are in operator notes outside the repo (C:/Users/<user>/freellmapi/SETUP-STATE.md "not backed up anywhere" and the client_profiles reading; PORT-BACKLOG §A env precedence), 1 is staleness in docs/history/alternatives-review-2026-08-09.md (sticky sessions, true when written 2026-08-09, overtaken by fde98ed on 2026-08-14), and 1 is a genuine misreading in docs/history/freellmapi-adoption-review-2026-08-13.md — freellmapi's `modelRetirementSignal` is a disjunction (C:\Code\freellmapi\server\src\lib\error-classify.ts:451,458: `const gone = status === 410 || ...; if (gone || (isModelNotFoundError(err) && END_OF_LIFE_PHRASES.some(...)))`), so a bare 410 is 'definitive' on its own and the status-AND-wording conjunction holds only on the 404 branch.
materialFindings.affects: DOC AUDIT headline "106 TRUE, 22 PARTIAL, 0 FALSE"
materialFindings.correction: Keep "0 FALSE out of 128" verbatim — it is true of that set. Add the all-claims line: 5 FALSE out of 375. No llm-relay decision moves: llm-relay's own 410 seed (src\refusal-interpretation.ts:480-486) requires 410 AND end-of-life wording, which is the stricter and rubric-4-correct choice regardless of what freellmapi does, and a bare uninterpreted 410 still fails over because 410 is in the retriable class at src\server.ts:1069.

tally: 375 claims total (128 prior + 247 new — note the brief's \"373\" is two short of 128+247). TRUE 282 (106 prior + 176 new), PARTIAL 88 (22 + 66), FALSE 5 (0 + 5), UNVERIFIABLE 0 as formally recorded. Caveat on the PARTIALs: roughly 14 of the 66 new ones are PARTIAL only because one half is a one-shot runtime measurement no source read can reconstruct (vitest run counts, a DB byte size, a \"14 commits behind\" fetch count, a token-cost ratio with no surviving artifact) — those halves are effectively UNVERIFIABLE rather than wrong, and settling them would require re-running the named suite or reading the live DB. Roughly 30 more are PARTIAL purely by staleness against a pinned commit, where the doc was correct on its own date.
